answers.text: The reply puts the fixes in priority order and says what needs a person
answers.evidence: The fixes are in tiers: 'Fix these before launch' (1-8, with problems 1 to 3 named as the ones that can stop a member reserving), then 'Fix soon after' (9-14) and 'Smaller items', plus a 'What I'd do first' list. The reply says 'I could not drive a real browser or a screen reader in this session', marks findings that depend on rendering as estimates, and asks for each fix to be run 'on a real phone with dark mode on, and with VoiceOver'.

mapping.title: Closed days can be picked; refused only at Confirm, with no way back
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R1, B R1). Same as D06: the calendar on the tool page lets a member pick a closed day with no warning. The refusal ('the library is closed that day') comes only after tapping Confirm reservation, and the day 'can't be changed from the basket or the confirm page', so the member has to go back to the tool page and redo every step.

mapping.title: Days before the tool's 'Available from' date are never checked
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R2, B R2). D14: nothing marks, disables or checks the days before the 'Available from' date, so 'the sander is available from 21 October, but you can reserve it for 10 October'. This is the same fault as the ground truth's tile-saw example.

mapping.title: Tool-page pick-up day and basket session can disagree
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R3, B R3). D15: the day picked on the tool page and the session picked in the basket 'are separate choices' that nothing reconciles, so the confirm page can say 'pick up Saturday 17 October' for the tool and 'Wednesday 21 October' for the session.

mapping.title: Unannounced 10-minute basket hold ends in a generic error that retries can't clear
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R4, B R4). D10: the basket says only 'Items are held for you while you finish' and shows no time, and after ten minutes Continue shows only 'Something went wrong. Try again.' The point that retrying never helps belongs to the same lapse handling. The review's fix (state the limit, say plainly when it runs out, offer to hold the tools again) fixes D10.

mapping.title: Tool names cut to one line, so the two drills look identical on a phone
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R5, B R5). D03: names are forced onto one line and cut off with an ellipsis, so at 375 px both drills read 'Cordless drill 18 V, c…' and 'two batteries' versus 'one battery' is hidden.

mapping.title: On phones the search form sits below all ten tool cards
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R6, B R6). D01: under 480 px the CSS 'moves the results above the search form', so a phone user has to scroll past every card to reach search and the date filter.

mapping.title: Filters button is an unlabelled three-line icon that looks like a menu
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R7, B R7). D01 names the three-line icon button, which has no text, as the only way to the date and category filters. The review's visible 'Filters' label is a narrower fix for the same problem: members not finding the filters.

mapping.title: Desktop keyboard order said to reach the results before the search form
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R8, B R8). Wrong as stated: D01 gives the document order as form then results, and the reorder applies only at 480 px and below. At desktop width, focus reaches search first, so no one has to 'tab through all ten tool links before reaching search'. The real order mismatch is the phone reorder, which is already R6 (D01).

mapping.title: A search with no matches leaves the old list and says nothing
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R9, B R9). D02: 'if nothing matches, the old list stays on screen, and screen readers hear nothing', so the member cannot tell whether the search ran or found nothing.

mapping.title: Search said to match only exact phrases ('battery' vs 'batteries')
mapping.reason: Settled (A R10 not-a-problem, B R10 real-unseeded; see settled). The review claims a member searching 'battery' 'sees the full list unchanged' because 'whole phrases are matched exactly'. Its own evidence contradicts this: one drill's name ends 'one battery', which contains 'battery'. Its fix, 'Match each word separately', would not make 'battery' match 'batteries' either. The no-results part is D02 (R9).

mapping.title: Confirm form rejects normal membership and mobile number formats
mapping.reason: Settled alignment (A R11 and R12, both D17; B R11, D17; see settled). D17: the membership number must be exactly 'FT-' plus five digits in capitals and the mobile '0xxxx xxxxxx', with no normalising. So 'Ft-01234' (iPhone capitalisation), 'FT01234', 'FT 01234', '+44 7700 900123' (autofill) and '07700 900 123' are all rejected.

mapping.title: Double tap on Confirm reservation books the tool twice
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R13, B R12). D12: the button stays active during the 1.5-second wait and nothing visible changes ('only aria-busy changes'). Each tap allocates a new reservation number, so a double tap gives 'FT-4471 and FT-4472'.

mapping.title: Basket Continue also stays active with no visible change during its wait
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R14, B R13). This is neither D12 (the Confirm button and its double booking) nor D10 (the message when the hold has lapsed): 'Same pattern in the basket: Continue has the same wait.' Nothing visible changes while it waits, so a member on a phone cannot tell whether the tap registered. They tap again or think the site is stuck.

mapping.title: Dark-mode 'Available from' badge is 3.07:1 and has no visible shape
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R15, B R14). D04: in the dark theme the badge text #2f7d4a on #1d2622 is 3.07:1, below 4.5:1. The badge background matching the card comes from the same badge's dark-theme colour settings, and the same change fixes it (--color-ok and --color-ok-tint).

mapping.title: Pick-up sessions listed in reverse date order on phones
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R16, B R15). D11: row-reverse with wrap-reverse puts the earliest session last on screen although it comes first in the document, so arrow keys and screen readers 'run against what's on screen'.

mapping.title: After 'Reserve this tool' the toast is brief and nothing leads on to the basket
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R17, B R16). This is about the feedback after the press: the toast 'is visible for only 1.2 seconds', nothing on screen moves the member towards the basket, and the only way on is the small 'Basket (1)' link. It does not say the member believes the tool is reserved, so it goes to D07, not D26.

mapping.title: Fixed bottom action bar covers the focused day and the footer phone number
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R18, B R17). D08: the fixed bar is 72 px tall but the page leaves only 8 px of space below the content. A focused calendar day can scroll under the bar, and the desk phone number in the footer is partly hidden.

mapping.title: Loan-length list can't be left with Tab, or closed with Escape or a tap outside
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R19, B R18). D09: while the custom listbox is open, Tab and Shift+Tab only move between the options and Escape does nothing, so a keyboard user cannot leave without choosing. Not closing on a tap outside is the same fault: the list cannot be dismissed. The radio-button fix removes both.

mapping.title: 'Choose a pick-up day' error not announced; focus jumps to a closed day
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R20, B R19). D19: the error is in no live region and the calendar does not reference it, so screen readers don't announce it. Focus jumps to the first day, 'a closed Friday'.

mapping.title: After confirming, the basket stays full and the hold timer keeps running
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R21, B R20). D18: after 'Reservation confirmed' the basket still shows the confirmed tools. Clearing the basket and the timer on confirmation, as the review proposes, fixes it.

mapping.title: Done page opened without a reservation shows a made-up number
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R22, B R21). Not in the ground truth. A member who reopens the done page without a stored reservation sees 'a made-up number', FT-4471, presented as a real confirmation. They may believe a tool is waiting, or quote that number at the desk.

mapping.title: Reservation numbers look like membership numbers
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R23, B R22). Not in the ground truth. Both are 'FT-' plus digits (FT-4471, FT-01234), so a member can give the desk the wrong one, or type a reservation number into the membership field and have it rejected.

mapping.title: Done page reads the tool name twice to screen readers
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R24, B R23). D24: the visually hidden '#c-tool' copy next to the visible list item makes screen readers read the reserved tool's name twice.

mapping.title: Confirm page 'Change' link's name doesn't say what it changes
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R25, B R24). Not D13, which is about Change dropping the chosen session; renaming the link would not fix that. A screen-reader member who tabs to the link or lists the page's links hears only 'Change' and cannot tell it is for the pick-up session.

mapping.title: Results grid's 330 px minimum column scrolls sideways at 320 px and 200% zoom
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R26, B R25). Exactly D05: the 330 px minimum column overflows the content box at 320 px and at 200% zoom, so the page scrolls sideways.

mapping.title: 'Up to three tools at a time' isn't enforced
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R27, B R26). D21: nothing checks the stated three-tool limit, so the basket takes a fourth tool and the reservation is confirmed.

mapping.title: Done-page fallback points to a confirmation text members aren't told about
mapping.reason: Agreed (A R28, B R27). Not in the ground truth. The fallback says 'See your confirmation text', but members are only told about texts for late returns. A member who sees it looks for a message they were never promised and is left without their reservation details.

settled.reason: Mapping decision. Both graders list the item, so it stays. The review says 'battery' doesn't match 'batteries' because 'whole phrases are matched exactly', so a member searching 'battery' 'sees the full list unchanged', and it proposes 'Match each word separately'. The review's own evidence contradicts this. It says the two drills differ by 'two batteries' vs 'one battery' (D03: 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, one battery'). Under the phrase matching it describes, 'battery' is found in that drill's name, so the list does change. And a one-word query behaves the same under phrase or per-word matching, so the fix would not make 'battery' find 'batteries'. The chat message keeps only the no-match case ('Searching for a word that isn't there ... leaves the old list on screen with no message'), which is D02 (R9). B's harm is that members who type another word form or word order miss tools the library has. The review does not show this: it gives no word-order case, and its word-form example does not behave as it says. The mapping instructions put 'wrong, speculative without basis in what the review shows' under not-a-problem, so A's value stands. This also matches how both graders treated R8, the other claim the evidence contradicts.

settled.a: R11 tool-library-D17 (membership number) and R12 tool-library-D17 (mobile number): two items
settled.b: R11 tool-library-D17 (membership and mobile number together): one item
settled.final: R11 tool-library-D17: one item, as B
settled.reason: Alignment decision. The review raises this as one problem. It is numbered once (problem 6) under the heading 'The confirm form rejects normal phone input', the 'What I'd do first' list calls it 'the form's input formats', and the chat message restates it once as 'The confirm form rejects normal input.' Its two bullets show the same fault in two fields: a fixed format that is never tidied ('must be exactly FT- plus five digits, in capitals'; 'must be 0xxxx xxxxxx'). They share one fix, 'Accept these formats and tidy them up yourself'. That is one distinct problem, not two different problems in one paragraph, so it is one item; splitting it by field would count one reported problem twice. Both graders kept the review's other sub-points as one item where they share a cause and a fix (the badge's text and background colours in problem 8; Tab, Escape and the outside tap in problem 12). They split only sub-points with a different cause, control or page (problems 1, 4, 7 and 14). D17 also covers both fields as one defect. The defect-level result is the same either way (D17). From here on, consensus R12–R27 are A's R13–R28 and B's R12–R27.
